newsitem.title: USA: Merrill upgrades Peru when-issued Brady bonds.
newsitem.headline: Merrill upgrades Peru when-issued Brady bonds.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co said it has upgraded its recommendation on Peru when-issued Brady bonds to market weight from underweight, reflecting, in part, the country's improving economic fundamentals and the pending closing of the Brady agreement on March 7.

"We believe that the price softening combined with the improving economic fundamentals and pending closing of the Brady agreement on March 7 make valuations for Peruvian Brady bonds more attractive and we are upgrading our recommendation to market weight from underweight," Joyce Chang, first vice president and manager of emerging markets of Merrill, said in a statement.
According to Merrill, the launching of an inaugural eurobond issue should also provide support for Peru Bradys.

"After the Brady agreement closes, Peru intends to tap the international capital markets to establish a benchmark, but government officials point out that a new bond issue is not necessary to meet financing requirements," Chang said in the Merrill report.
Merrill also believes Peru's overall macroeconomic picture this year should show marked improvement over the performance in 1996, with growth of around 4.0 to 5.0 percent in 1997.
